body.x: Steve Koenig, the Director of Industry Analysis for the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), gave a presentation on the past, present, and future of global technology market at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

To prepare this report, CEA collaborated with GfK (Gesellschaft für Konsumforschung-Society for Consumer Research) and CE MarketMetrics. GfK is Germany's largest market research institute and the fourth largest market research organization in the world, and tracked retail consumer electronics sales at more than 340,000 retail stores in 80 countries, and CE MarketMetrics makes a monthly tracking/forecasting of shipment to U.S. consumer sales channels for dozens of CE categories.

What technologies are driving spending growth? According to the report, smartphones remain as the spending driver. From 2011 to 2013, spending of all consumer electronics increased only $10 billion dollars, from $1,007 billion to $1,017 billion, but for smartphone, the consumer spending almost doubled from $181 billion to $331 billion.

The technology's seven magnificent devices are as follows: tablet PC, digital still camera, desk PC, mobile PC, LCD TV, mobile phone and smartphone. The share from the seven devices is expected to increase from 72% in 2011 to 80% in 2014. However, the share from smartphone is expected to increase 22%, from 18% in 2011 to 40% in 2015.

Among the smaller products, the sales of video game consoles is expected to increase from 2014, from $19 billion in 2014 and $21 billion 2015. The smaller products are defined as follows: CRT TV, inkjet printer & mfd, laser printer & mfd, car navigation, camcorder, plasma TV, DVD player/recorder, portable media player, monitor, video games console, inkjet cartridge, laser cartridge, and home audio.
Smartphone and tablets are claiming more spending share. In 2011, only 22% took the share from global tech device sales revenue. In 2015, the share is expected to increase 46%.

New innovations such as smartwatches, health & fitness tech, smart home technologies and automotive technologies are rapidly entering the global stage. Globally, smartphone unit sales in 2010 was 267.3 million units but has been increasing rapidly. In 2014, the estimates sales of smartphones is 1,273.7 million and in 2015, the number will increase 19% to 1,509.8 million units.

Emerging markets are taking the biggest share in the sales. While the percentage of sales in mature market has decreased from 60% in 2010 to 32% in 2013, that of developing market has increased from 40% to 68% during the same period. Globally, the revenue of smartphone was $117,717 million. It is expected to grow to $406,735 million in 2015.

The unit sales of tablet was 15.8 million units in 2010. But in 2015, it is expected to increase to 337 million units. Also for tablets, developing market is the driving force of the sales. In 2011, only 21% of all tablet sales came from the developing markets. It is expected to increase to 44% in 2015.

The latest trend in tablet are as follows. Tablets that enables taking notes on it, known as "phablets," will hit the market. Affordable android tablets in $100 US dollar range and tablets with a new Intel M processors will also be released.

The sales of TV is expected to grow slowly after a drastic fall in 2012. It hit 262 million units in 2011 but dropped to 242 million units in 2012. But in 2013, it came back to 243 million units. The estimated sales of TV in 2015 is 251 million units.

The average screen size in U.S. markets in 1997 was 22 inches. In 2014, it is 42 inches. Now, the market is moving to 4K Ultra HD TV. In 2013, the sales of 4K TV took only 0.9% of all TV sales, but in 2014, it took 9.3% of the market. It is expected to soar up to 23.3% in 2015.

In summary, 2014 global technology spending went up 1% to $1,024 trillion. Emerging Asia region, led by China, now leads tech spending with $282 trillion in 2014. For now, global consumer tech spending remains driven by mobile, connected devices, with no guarantee.
